facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified
A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration with foamy histiocytes and Touton-like giant cells is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease.
The patient's radiographic findings and histiocytic infiltration could also suggest Langerhans cell histiocytosis, although the absence of CD1a and langerin staining makes this less likely.

The patient's presentation of elevated inflammatory markers and enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues could suggest sarcoidosis, although the absence of granulomas makes this less likely.
The patient's radiographic findings could suggest bone metastasis, although the absence of malignant cells and negative tumor markers make this less likely.
The patient's radiographic findings could suggest Paget's disease of bone, although the absence of characteristic bone deformities and elevated alkaline phosphatase makes this less likely.

rationales.F01: Diffuse bone pain is a non-specific symptom that does not strongly suggest any particular diagnosis.
rationales.F03: Exophthalmos and blurred vision are suggestive of Erdheim-Chester disease due to orbital involvement.
rationales.F06: Sclerotic bone changes are characteristic of Erdheim-Chester disease.
rationales.F09: Enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues are highly suggestive of Erdheim-Chester disease.
rationales.F10: Diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells is diagnostic of Erdheim-Chester disease.
rationales.F11: Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease.
